# Background

Your Cuban uncle sets up a cocktail bar in downtown Budapest. He has a secret list of cocktails that he would like to serve in the bar. He asks you to do create a few lists and tables to set up the shop. As your uncle is a secret hipster, he has a dataset on Github that you can use for the task!

![](https://media1.tenor.com/images/57a519cffd0ad4693be3b9c94b211540/tenor.gif?itemid=5195211){width="320"}

Note: There are several different ways to solve these tasks, feel free to come up with your own.

## 1. Read the data

Read the cocktail dataset from: <https://github.com/nthun/cocktail-balance> You can also find the codebook there.

```{r include=FALSE}
rpath <- "/home/equarius/Downloads/cocktail_data.tsv"
rd <- as.data.frame(read_tsv(rpath))
```

## 2. Transform the data table and clean the ingredient variable!

The ingredients are currently in a single cell for each cocktail. It would be better to put them in separate rows. Also, the variable should be cleaned of all quantities (e.g. 1/2 oz, 2 dashes, etc.), and the indicator of alcohol content (e.g. 47.3% abv). You will need to use this cleaned table in later tasks.

```{r include=FALSE}
#split ingredients with strsplit, add them as new rows
rd2 <- rd
rnum <- seq(1:nrow(rd2))
rd2$ingredients <- gsub("<br>","<br/>",rd2$ingredients)
for(temprow in rnum){ #loop through rows
  tempnam <- as.character(rd2[temprow,1])
  tempingr <- rd2 %>% 
    filter(name==tempnam) %>% 
    select(ingredients) %>% 
    as.character()
  if(grepl("<br.>", tempingr)){ #if ingredient contains line break
    tempingra <- unlist(strsplit(tempingr,split="<br.>")) #split it according to <br/>
    for(temping in tempingra){ #loop through the split-up ingredients and add them as separate rows
      mytemprow <- rd2[temprow,]
      mytemprow$ingredients <- temping
      rd2 <- rbind(rd2,mytemprow)
    }
  }
}
rd2 <- rd2[56:nrow(rd2),] #get rid of the original rows
row.names(rd2) <- 1:nrow(rd2)
for(temprow in (1:nrow(rd2))){ #loop through rows
  tempingr <- rd2[temprow,"ingredients"]
  print(rd2[temprow,1])
  cat("The ingredient is",tempingr,"\n",sep=" ")
  tempingr <- unlist(strsplit(tempingr, split = " "))[c(-1,-2)] #get rid of first 2 words, which are the quantities
  tempingr <- paste(tempingr[!grepl(paste(seq(1,9),"%","abv","/","oz",sep="|",collapse="|"),tempingr)], collapse = " ") #get rid of alcohol content if there is
  cat("The ingredient is",tempingr,"\n",sep=" ")
  rd2[temprow,"ingredients"] <- tempingr
  
}
cld <- rd2 #get cleaned table for later use
```

## 3. All ingredients in alphabetical order

Before opening the bar, you need to find a reliable supplier that has all the ingredients. You need to send a list of all possible ingredients you will need. They don't need the quantities (i.e. how many of these are needed), just the names of the ingredients.

```{r include=FALSE}
ingrlist<-sort(unique(unlist(strsplit(unique(cld$ingredients),split=" or "))))
```

## 4. Number of unique ingredients

How many different ingredients you will need?

We are going to need `r length(ingrlist)` ingredients.
```{r}
#see the above cell
```

## 5. What are the top 10 ingredients?

What are the 10 most frequently used ingredients? If there are ties, you can list more than 10.

```{r include=FALSE}
test <- cld %>% 
  select(ingredients) %>% 
  mutate(ingredients = as.factor(ingredients)) %>%
  group_by(ingredients) %>% 
  summarize(numb=n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(numb)) %>% 
  filter(numb>=unique(numb)[10])
head(test, n = 10)
```
The 10 most frequently used ingredients are: `r paste(ingrlist[as.numeric(unlist(head(test, n = 10)[1]))], collapse=",")`.

## 6. Which cocktail(s) has/have the most ingredients?

Count the number of ingredients and filter all the cocktails that has that many.

```{r include=FALSE}
most <- cld %>% 
  mutate(name = as.factor(name)) %>% 
  group_by(name) %>% 
  summarize(numb = n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(numb)) %>% 
  filter(numb==max(numb))
```

The cocktails with the most amount of ingredients are: `r paste(unlist(most$name),collapse=", ")`.

## 7. How many ingredients appear in only one cocktail (rare ingredient)?

Count all cocktails with only one ingredient, and

```{r include=FALSE}
rare <- cld %>% 
  select(ingredients) %>% 
  mutate(ingredients = as.factor(ingredients)) %>%
  group_by(ingredients) %>% 
  summarize(numb=n()) %>% 
  arrange(numb) %>% 
  filter(numb==min(numb))
  
```

There are `r nrow(rare)` rare ingredients, which appear only once.

## 8. Which cocktail has an ingredient that is only used in one cocktail?

```{r include=FALSE}
rarecocktail <- unique(cld[which(cld$ingredients %in% rare$ingredients),"name"])
```

The following cocktails have rare ingredients: `r paste(unlist(rarecocktail),sep=",",collapse=",")`

## 9. What are the cocktails without rare ingredients?

```{r include=FALSE}
withoutrare <-  unique(cld[!(cld$name %in% rarecocktail),"name"])
```

The following cocktails don't have rare ingredients: `r paste(unlist(withoutrare),sep=",",collapse=",")`

## 10. Create a cheat sheet for the bartender!

Create a matrix that shows all cocktail names as rows and all ingredients as columns. When a cocktail requires an ingredient, there should be an "X" in the cell, otherwise, the cell should remain empty. Example:

```{r echo=FALSE}
tribble(~name, ~Lime, ~`White rum`, ~`Cane sugar`, ~`Coca-cola`, ~Mint, ~Soda,
        "Caipirissima", "X", "X", "X", "", "", "",
        "Cuba Libre", "X", "X", "", "X","","",
        "Mojito", "X", "X", "", "", "X", "X") %>% 
    relocate(name, sort(names(.)))
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
chs <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow=nrow(rd),ncol=length(ingrlist)+1))
chs[,1] <- unique(rd$name)
colnames(chs) <- c("name",ingrlist)
for(temprow in (1:nrow(cld))){
  tempingr <- cld[temprow,"ingredients"]
  tempname <- cld[temprow,"name"]
  chs[chs$name==tempname,tempingr] <- "X"
}
chs[is.na(chs)] <- ""
```
